title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative: A strategic compliance plan was developed by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA) in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), in consultation with the social partners, and piloted in the iron and steel, in the industrial sector, and pomegranate and grape in agriculture. The ILO conducted relevant capacity building programmes for 20 inspectors and senior labour inspection officials on the relevant issues, and provided technical guidance and advice on the development of the plan and relevant awareness-raising material.

description.narrative:
The Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA) in Baghdad, and the one in the Kurdstan Region of Iraq (KRI), developed a National Labour Inspection Policy, in consultation with the social partners, which was officially endorsed and launched in November 2022.
MOLSA in Erbil developed a new labour law which was adopted by KRI parliament in March 2023.
The following tools were also developed by MOLSA, in both regions, to enhance labour inspection effectiveness: - A “Guide to Labour Inspection in Agriculture-Iraq 2022”.. - Updated all checklists and templates used in labour inspection and OSH, which incorporated gender issues and health emergencies, including epidemics. - A comprehensive national labour inspection training plan The ILO provided technical support for drafting the strategy and validating it with the social partners and other stakeholders.
The ILO provided inputs and comments for the development of the new law
The ILO drafted the new labour inspection tools (Guide, checklists and templates) in consultation with MOLSA and finalized them based on the feedback received from the labour inspectorate and social partners.
The ILO draft the new labour inspection training plan, based on a proper training needs assessment, and finalized it based on discussions with MOLSA.

description.narrative: The Tripartite Coordination Council was established and held an ad hoc meeting on August 17, 2023, headed by the Minister of Labour, with the participation of representatives of all Iraqi trade unions and the head of the Iraqi Federation of Industries. The discussion held in the Council facilitated the resolution of conflicts between different Trade Unions and resulted in initiation of a process of drafting of a new Trade Union Law, which is in line with the ILO standards. The ILO organized a workshop on 14-15 Sep. 2023 to facilitate the work of the tripartite Coordination Council in discussing the new draft trade union law in Iraq, with the participation of the Parliamentary Labour Committee, the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, and the trade unions, in addition to a representative of the Iraqi Federation of Industries.

description.narrative: The government of Iraq and Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) have developed, endorsed and launched National OSH Policy and Profile, in addition to a comprehensive Capacity Building Plan, in November 2022. These documents aimed at promoting their preventive services in line with international labour standards. This includes in designing workplaces, the work environment, tools, machines, equipment, chemical, physical and biological factors and working methods, including testing, maintaining, replacing, installing and arranging them. Moreover, consideration of the relationship between the physical elements of work and the people who carry them out, with the aim of adapting machines, equipment and working times. The national OSH policy also includes protecting workers and their representatives from disciplinary measures for taking measures to preserve their safety, providing training with the aim of achieving work in safe ways as well as cooperation between the work team and the facility. The National Centre for Occupational Safety and Health (NCOSH) has strengthened its capabilities for monitoring workplace environmental hazards and equipped itself with portable tools and equipment during inspection visits. With the support of the European Union (EU), the ILO has provided technical inputs in the development and update of OSH Policy and Profile, Capacity Building and Action Plan, aiming to improve preventative services in workplace. Furthermore, the ILO facilitated consultations with tripartite partners MoLSA, workers and employers to assess, review, validate and develop comprehensive national OSH Policy and Profile. The ILO provided technical support and assistance to the NCOSH to strengthen its capabilities in particular in monitoring environmental hazards.

description.narrative: The government of Iraq and Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) have improved and modernized their OSH systems and enhanced their effectiveness through development, updating and promoting their national recording and notification mechanisms of work-related accidents and injuries. Reporting and recording tools and templates were developed and updated in close consultation with representatives of social partners. The national recording and notification system of work-related accidents and injuries provides annual data, which is gender-disaggregated. With the support of the European Union (EU), and in collaboration of the International Training Centre of ILO in Turin (ITC-ILO), the ILO provided technical inputs to the development of OSH program, and recording and notification mechanism and reporting templates. Other activities included capacity building workshop and knowledge sharing on recording and notification systems in other countries.
